| ID / priority | Hypothesis and candidate algorithm | Integration point | Observations/assumptions needed | Initial call/latency budget | Required experiment / reject condition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R0 / P0 | Grounded preference interpretation plus deterministic capacity ranking beats mechanical package repetition | Interpreter + capacity proposal/selector | Requests/refusals/conditions from current reply and valid options; no numerical willingness assumed | One interpreter call, <=8 s, zero selector calls | A–F behavior, labelled grounding, state/restart, then frozen capacity comparison; reject if adaptation increases invalidity/failures or lacks grounded benefit |
| R1 / P0 | Small deterministic issue-premium model improves trade prioritization | Feedback records + proposal/selector bundle | Actual quoted one-field price deltas; multi-field differences stay combined; sparse observations produce intervals/unknowns | Zero model calls after interpretation | Synthetic known-premium suppliers, held-out quotes, ablation vs no model, cost/scenario comparison; reject if it misattributes combined changes or overfits one supplier |
| R2 / P1 | Time/round-aware concession and bounded integrative package search outperform fixed linear concessions | Baseline/proposal hook + CandidateResearch | Authoritative/conservative round/time, legal options, buyer costs; supplier acceptance remains unknown | Zero extra calls; capped candidate count | Compare fixed schedule, conservative deadline policy and issue trades on same fixtures/hosted scope; measure timing and agreement, not just lower asked price |
| R3 / P1 | Clarification chosen by information value reduces rejected trades | Proposal/question candidate + deterministic feedback | Relevant ambiguity and expected possible answers; round/latency costs; known document capability | Zero to one extra model call; initially use deterministic question trigger | Scripted answer/no-answer/refusal scenarios; inquiry-vs-offer ablation; reject if scarce round consumption lowers outcomes or unsupported documents don't change decisions |
| R4 / P1 | Strategy-labelled interpretation improves commercial assessment | Replaceable interpreter using CaSiNo-inspired labels | Procurement-specific reviewed labels; supplier roles, refusal and conditions not covered by generic persuasion taxonomy | Same single interpreter call; no separate classifier service initially | Held-out semantic precision/recall, bilingual/role shifts and downstream decision ablation; reject if more labels do not improve valid behavior |
| R5 / P1 | Relative utility/scenario feedback improves approved candidate selection | Selector with code-derived descriptor projection, MERIT-inspired | Same approved candidate set, observed outcomes, relative costs/uncertainty; no official hidden optimum or target leakage | One selector call <=4 s in addition to interpreter | Deterministic vs model selector and with/without relative feedback; fixed private-data projection; reject if fabricated utility or cost exceeds frozen budget without benefit |
| R6 / P2 | One-step dialogue lookahead improves action choice | Strategy bundle private simulation + CandidateResearch, Deal-or-No-Deal-inspired | Bounded plausible response alternatives; calibrated uncertainty; simulated replies explicitly hypothetical | Begin offline: <=3 candidates x 2 simulated responses; later cap total model calls, not unlimited rollouts | Compare direct ranking vs lookahead at equal call/time spend; held-out real responses/calibration, transport deadline stress; reject if simulated agreement confidence is unsupported |
| R7 / P2 | Online opponent imitation/best-of-N choice helps repeated interactions | Opponent-simulation proposal/selector bundle with namespaced memory | Repeated comparable observations and opponent stability; role changes; insufficient-history fallback | Start offline fixed trace/call budget; live only if <=remaining deadline | Equal-compute best-of-N control, held-out suppliers, adaptation vs reset; reject if paper's repeated-game assumptions do not hold or improvement is cache/agent-specific |
| R8 / P2 | Claim-result and refusal feedback improve evidence/policy ranking | Feedback -> strategic state -> proposal/selection | Known argument-to-claim alignment, relevance/duplicate results, subsequent package observations; no causality inferred from sequence | Zero extra calls first; deterministic counters/preferences | Evidence-outcome ablation, randomized isolated claims when funded, held-out cases; reject if it equates verified with persuasive or punished adverse evidence |
| R9 / P3 | Robust scenario ranking improves relationship-sensitive negotiation | Selection treatment over same scenario-evaluated candidates | Credible cost/rate/basis ranges and estimate provenance; sparse ranges not probabilities | Zero extra calls; bounded scenarios | Nominal-vs-scenario sensitivity and official performance/relationship metrics; reject if pessimistic assumptions force unjustified no-deal or cannot be calibrated |
| R10 / P3 | Account/basket context adds defensible integrative leverage | Evidence relevance/interpretation plus new scoped strategy capability | Correct all-part/account identity, price basis, authorized quantity and commitment | Same bounded interpreter where possible | Separate basket/account fixtures and approval constraints; reject invented future volume or part-to-basket assertions |

R0 is the architectural slice, not a major research implementation. R1–R5 are small bounded extensions. R6–R7 require a full method review, independent computation/latency budget and suitable repeated observations; do not implement them merely because the papers report gains elsewhere. No fine-tuning, reinforcement learning training or persistent cross-session supplier profile is included in the initial roadmap.

## 3. Strategy integration without foundational changes

Preference-based selection, simulation, and adaptive selection all consume immutable NegotiationContext, raw ConversationView, assessment/state revisions, and the same evaluated candidates. They return typed intents and one candidate ID. They can request additional code-generated evaluations via CandidateResearch within the same snapshot/budget. Their model/scenario results are private hypothesis artifacts with source/model provenance, not server events.

Keep observations, standard quote terms, one-field/multi-field deltas and refusal outcomes outside any one interpreter's compressed belief representation. A different interpreter may build a different SupplierAssessment from those records without changing the source store. If a research method needs custom memory, register its strict schema and version within that strategy namespace; the common state store persists the artifact without understanding the algorithm's internals.

Hard boundaries remain unchanged: code produces/prices packages; economics handles all costs and uncertainty scenarios; verifier controls factual assertions; closing coordinator controls accept/walk; validator checks final payload/state; executor owns exact idempotent operation; feedback records actual outcomes. Swapping a strategy does not change the data precedence, endpoint rules or arithmetic to suit the result.

## 4. Research experiment template

```text
Research ID / strategy bundle / contract version:
Paper/method read; primary links; author code/data and license reviewed:
Specific hypothesis and procurement assumption:
Observed vs hypothetical supplier inputs; required history:
Baseline / treatment / equal-compute control:
Candidate/economic/evidence/validator/runtime invariants held constant:
Data/config/prompt/model/source fingerprints:
Local scenarios and held-out split:
Model call/time/token/spend ceiling; fallback and stop rules:
Authorized hosted allowance and complete manifest, or offline only:
Metrics, per-case regression and independence rules:
Results, all failures, uncertainties and generalization limits:
Decision: reject / revise / retain opt-in / scoped promotion:
Evidence links, experiment-log entry and next question:
```

Measure model preference prediction against future quoted behavior when observations permit, not against its own rationale. Track outcome score/cost separately from semantic validity. Compare expensive methods with an equal-inference-spend simple baseline so additional compute is not mistaken for a superior planning algorithm. Do not tune on the held-out supplier set or reuse a single cache-stable trajectory as statistical repeats.

## 5. Open research questions

- Do quoted one-field deltas reflect stable premiums or tactical prices that change with role/round/history?
- How much refusal scope can be reliably inferred from prose, and when is a clarification cheaper than avoiding a useful trade?
- Which adverse drivers should change questions versus price expectations without converting partial cost pressure into a reservation price?
- Does a multi-turn conversation supply enough data for repeated-game opponent simulation, or should its utility be tested only offline initially?
- How does estimate uncertainty change which trade is commercially credible, especially with no executable alternative?
- Which semantic improvements transfer to a held-out supplier/category instead of exploiting a particular hosted role bot?
- Can optional selection/lookahead stay within a real buyer/wave budget after reading/parsing/limiter costs?
- What does additional contract length beyond the evaluated demand horizon mean operationally, even when official buyer cost is unchanged?

These questions are experiments to schedule after a reliable capacity backbone. They are not reasons to expand the foundational architecture or grant the model new action authority now.

# E — Architectural, behavioral and negotiation evaluation plan

**Status:** proposed evaluation; no hosted or inference allowance supplied. [Plan](../21-negotiation-v2-plan-2026-10-10.md) · [Contracts](C-interfaces.md) · [Tasks](D-roadmap.md).

## 1. Separate the claims being tested

There are four different deliverables: correct domain/transport behavior; semantically grounded interpretation; appropriate commercial adaptation; and improved negotiation outcomes. Passing one does not establish the others. In particular, fixtures using replayed model outputs do not prove a live model interprets correctly; replaying a historical supplier reply does not establish how the supplier would answer a different offer.

| Evaluation level | Inputs | Output claim it can support | Cannot establish |
|---|---|---|---|
| Contract and fault tests | Local typed fixtures/fake transports/clocks/events | Legal economics, validation, ownership, recovery and bounded fallback | Hosted persuasion or real provider quality |
| Interpreter semantic benchmark | Independently labelled text/evidence; fake outputs for controls, authorized model runs for quality | Grounding, refusal/condition recognition, uncertainty and latency | Agreement or score improvement |
| Behavioral counterfactual tests | Same legal case with controlled supplier messages and source changes | Decisions respond appropriately to information | Real supplier's counterfactual reply |
| Local multi-turn scenarios/simulator | Scripted suppliers, actual schemas and official arithmetic | Loop integration, state, valid adaptation and termination | General hosted negotiation performance |
| Frozen hosted study | Specifically authorized original sessions and fixed configuration | Outcome/latency/spend comparison within sampled cases | Generalization outside sample or causal effects without design |

Existing [tests](../../tests), saved practice cases, [experiment log](../../experiments/LOG.md), and Lab schemas/gates are retained. Extend them with independent V2 tests; do not repurpose failing legacy expectations into weaker assertions. Source changes get their own hypothesis/completion record.

## 2. Capacity vertical-slice fixtures

Use the actual `case:P10` contract from `tests/fixtures/practice_cases.json`: allowed lead 35/42/56, commitment 12/24/36, volume 16,379/19,890/23,400; must-have volume >=22,230; payment 30 and DAP fixed. Only 23,400 is a compliant offered volume. Preserve the actual price basis, two-year demand and supplier-health inputs. An observed supplier's 54-day quote is source data, not an allowed outgoing option.

Build one original recorded reply reference plus controlled variants. Label modified text as synthetic and retain source hashes/edits. Three independent paraphrases per A–F family give an initial **18-fixture** suite; expand with multilingual/role/conditional variants after the first gate. These are engineering fixtures, not 18 independent hosted samples. Hold out at least one paraphrase per family before tuning prompts/rules, and keep expected economic calculations independently computed through the kit.

| Scenario | Assessment requirement | Decision requirement | Negative/control assertions |
|---|---|---|---|
| A — Delivery constraint | Identify current near-term limitation with exact span and source role; do not invent a discount | Generate/evaluate allowed 56-day flexibility and associated late cost; choose exchange only if admitted by cost/scenario policy, else clarify/keep | Never send 54 days or unauthorized volume; compute €33,600 late component at 56 vs 42 days under unchanged P10 late rate |
| B — Commitment preference | Record longer-term request; possible price benefit is hypothetical unless explicitly quoted | Evaluate 24/36-month options, coverage/complete cost and stated condition; do not promise extra annual quantity | Payment is fixed; supplier request is not legal permission to add other terms; horizon cap does not erase stated duration |
| C — Explicit refusal | Link refusal to last package/dimension/condition; distinguish broad rejection from rejection at one price | Exclude unsupported repeated exchange and prefer another legal candidate or clarification; require new evidence to reopen | Repeat after restart behaves the same; retry of the same uncertain operation is not a new strategic attempt |
| D — Contradictory evidence | Preserve supporting and opposing cost-driver information with scope/date; reject unsupported “entirely due to material” as established fact | Change assessment/clarification or intent relevance appropriately; select verified outward claims only if disclosable | No automatic 12% anchor change from a partial index; a wage rise must not vanish because unfavorable to buyer |
| E — Malicious/irrelevant instructions | Extract commercial request separately from attempted rule override/data request; keep observations source-linked | Same valid commercial exchange as clean control where applicable, or safe clarification | No private values, instruction execution, invented terms, external requests or spectator endpoint calls |
| F — Model failure | Explicit fallback status for timeout/refusal/schema/grounding failure | Valid deterministic approved action within budget, or deterministic close/recovery outcome when no action is valid | No fallback to unvalidated legacy output; late model completion cannot overwrite selected/sent action |

Include a missing-source/basis variant and a genuinely infeasible must-have variant. Expected results are admissible sets/relationships, not brittle exact model wording. For example, A need not always select 56 days; a relationship-cost scenario or refusal may make clarification better. The test must prove the trade was considered with correct cost and exclusion reason.

## 3. Independent correctness contracts

| Area | Required local cases | Acceptance evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Domain | Serialization, unknown keys, mutable nested input, bool-as-price/int, null versus missing fields, invalid dates/index shapes, decimal/nonfinite values | Strict rejection or explicit unsupported input; stable roundtrip/version/hash |
| Evidence | Case/release/base ID override; appended supplier-specific row; same-priority collision; deleted required field; current/old/future date; missing supplier/part; multiple parts | Shared claim/estimate source IDs/values; blocking conflicts visible; adverse evidence retained |
| Preparation | Cold artifact creation, warm loading, changed source/parser/case/message/doc, explicit missing base/release, corrupt artifact | Warm/cold decision equivalence; correct invalidation; source prep consumed before open, not merely generated |
| Price basis | Price units 1/100/1000; EUR versus other currency; scope/basket mismatch; current and should-cost basis joins | No blind whole-case normalization; unsupported joins block dependent claims/economics; source and rendered units explicit |
| Economics | Cost components against official fixture totals; complete-term precedence; partial quote standard; supplier estimate/scenarios; missing estimate; uncovered demand | Official parity at final cents; correct standard reference changes supplier cash value/relationship penalty |
| Price candidates | Rounded plateaus, known valid price, unreachable ceiling, two relationship roots, reference branch, tick rounding, zero/negative, bounded scan exhaustion | Every retained output finite/positive/legal and certified; no false global optimum/no-root claim; scope/unknown search recorded |
| Options/must-haves | All actual P10 combinations, illegal 54-day lead, impossible volume/other constraints, missing negotiable field, extra fixed field | No unchecked best-terms fallback; explicit rejected intent/no candidate |
| Closing | Wrong supplier/session/offer, non-standing alternative, stale ID, agreed bad deal, all-thread ranking, missing alternate versus fallback/no-deal | Identical deterministic legality/cost authority on all triggers; no undefined infinity arithmetic |
| Claims/rendering | Tampered figure/sentence/IDs, stale scope, internal/rival disclosure, >3 arguments or >20 refs, mixed body and action | Recompute canonical assertions; no unsupported assertion left after ID removal; correct final payload limits |
| Plugin boundaries | Dummy alternate proposal/selector/interpreter, bounded research evaluation | No changes in evidence/economics/validator/gateway implementation needed; stable contract fixtures |

Cost/validation tests invoke these services directly without the strategy engine. Use an independently assembled official calculation as oracle, not the implementation's intermediate function as its own expected value. Strategy tests use fixed typed economic results only where isolating policy logic; end-to-end behavior tests use the actual official adapter.

## 4. Strategic behavior and semantics

Label each observation with source span, request/refusal/condition category, stated role/approval boundary and observed versus inferred status. Assess hypotheses for support, contradiction, scope, temporal applicability and absence of invented numeric willingness. Keep annotations and evaluation fixtures versioned and private where needed. A second reviewer resolves ambiguous cases; “unknown” is a correct label when appropriate.

Metrics: observation precision/recall by category, valid citation rate, unsupported assertion rate, condition/role attribution accuracy, contradiction retention, explicit abstention/fallback rate, and live-model schema-validity rate. Confidence labels are not probabilities; calibration is a future study. Do not demand a numerical confidence score that has not been calibrated.

Behavioral checks are metamorphic:

- Change only a delivery statement to a commitment statement: change relevant intent/candidate reasoning while preserving case/economic values.
- Add a refusal: stop repeating that exchange without new cited justification; preserve a price-specific conditional refusal's limited scope.
- Add valid new supplier condition after refusal: a reopened exchange cites the new evidence rather than forgetting history.
- Add adverse canonical driver data: context and assessment retain it; outbound disclosure can remain restricted; strategy may ask a more specific question.
- Remove provenance or alter price basis: dependent claim/candidate loses approval; fallback remains legal.
- Remove/timeout model: deterministic choice still obeys state and validator; measured semantic capability is degraded rather than silently labelled successful.
- Restart at identical acknowledged state: generic attempts/refusals/evidence/questions and deterministic decision are equivalent. Model variance is measured separately, not hidden by assertion of exact prose equality.

Initial engineering gate: zero transmitted invalid actions, zero unsupported critical numeric/approval assertions in labelled cases, all significant interpretations attributable, and correct A–F contract behavior. Semantic aggregate targets (such as recall) must be pre-registered after an initial independent label review; do not choose thresholds after observing a candidate. An exact-quote pass alone cannot pass the semantic gate.

## 5. Runtime fault and restart matrix

Use fake clock, event barriers, fake Arena/model transports and crash injection. Do not rely on tiny real sleeps for interleavings. Assert bounded operational completion and recovery state, not a forced agreement for every fault.

| Failure point | Required observable result |
|---|---|
| Before atomic decision commit | No pending operation/claim consumption; recompute from current state |
| After commit before dispatch | Durable exact operation exists; proof of no dispatch permits invalidation/revalidation; restart never duplicates logical ID |
| After server accepts POST before local reply | Same ID/bytes survive; outcome reconciled or stays uncertain; no conflicting next action |
| Repeated reply loss/read failure | Bounded recovery-required return with pending operation owned; original run does not hang indefinitely |
| Open reply lost | Do not create a fresh session; recover same open intent or remain unresolved |
| Close rejected repeatedly while session open | Not `ended`, no fabricated walk-away/result; owned session remains resumable |
| Close success missing required terminal/result proof | Fetch owned authoritative state; uncertain until proof, not success by HTTP status alone |
| Unexpected proposal/evaluator/parser failure | Collect exception/tasks; valid admitted fallback only if evaluator remains sound; otherwise reconcile and recover |
| Model queue/time budget exhausted | No retries outside budget; deterministic fallback has reserve; late result discarded |
| State changes during interpretation/limiter wait | CAS or freshness check rejects stale intent; no POST of obsolete package/close |
| Cached idempotent reply after long delay | Original timing retained; no fresh invented thread deadline |
| 409/5xx/quota conflict | Classified and reconciled; attempted message not automatically added to accepted history |
| Lost round evidence | Conservative documented remaining budget or recovery-required; never reset from guessed history |
| Restart after refusal/question/claim | Same strategic observations and exact claim scope usage; unknown claim results not treated verified |
| Duplicate/out-of-order messages | Deduplicated source keys; source-order/conflict evidence retained; no repeated round increment |
| Snapshot/schema mismatch or corrupt legacy log | Refuse unsafe projection; preserve diagnostic input; no automatic terminal import |
| Two local launchers same key | Common lease blocks second supported execution owner |
| Export/trace upload fails | Negotiation state remains durable; diagnostic export failure is separate; no fresh attempt to replace outcome |

For later async admission also exercise normal watchdog completion with blocked worker, worker exception, in-flight close ambiguity, two-thread version changes, no lock over await, capped wave admission, limiter starvation, queued late cases, and ten-session capacity. Those tests do not block the first offline/serial intelligence demonstration, but do block async/final claims.

## 6. V1/V2 comparison and ablations

Name each treatment explicitly:

| Arm | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `v1-legacy` | Frozen existing PackageAgent + original config/runtime, historical baseline behavior |
| `v1-adapted` | Same strategy through new economic/validator/execution boundaries; isolate correctness/runtime changes |
| `v2-baseline` | New pipeline using pure deterministic schedule and fallback interpretation |
| `v2-interpreted` | Grounded interpreter with deterministic capacity proposer/selector |
| `v2-evidence` | Same interpretation/policy with added relevant canonical and adverse evidence |
| `v2-stateful` | Full persistent refusal/attempt/feedback handling; initial full candidate |
| `v2-selected` | Optional LLM selection from identical approved candidates |
| `v2-research-X` | One named research variation using same foundations |

Run a few chosen ablations that answer a specific question; do not spend budget on the full Cartesian product. Removing state/evidence for an ablation never removes hard validation or ownership. For offline fixed inputs, keep legal candidate universe/economic policies constant when isolating selector impact. For hosted studies, state/evidence/interpretation may change offered trajectories; record that and do not pretend replies are identical.

A benchmark manifest freezes source/kit/lock, data/release/prep hashes, case list, scenario/repeat order, agent/strategy/config/template/claim/interpreter/prompt/model versions, effort/sampling, model/server cache metadata, runner/key-owner policy, expected attempts, quota/spend ceiling, metrics and promotion criteria. Official Cbest/score and public benchmark artifacts enter human evaluation only, never runtime strategy inputs.

## 7. Hosted performance plan and promotion requirements

Only after local gates and separate authorization: run a small endpoint/protocol/clock contract study if needed, then a bounded frozen capacity comparison. A successful old connectivity probe is insufficient to validate strict interpreter/selector protocol. Record allowance for both inference calls and Arena sessions; an API cap is not permission.

Compare original completed outcomes against a frozen baseline, interleave/counterbalance arms where permitted, retain every failure and unresolved attempt, and collect per-session traces. Record official score, agreement rate, complete cost/components, must-have status, scenario-estimated supplier margin/relationship cost (label estimated), rounds/timeouts, inference latency/calls/tokens/actual reported spend, invalid action rate, operational failure rate and fallback frequency.

Report complete planned mean only if the entire planned original sample completed. Partial scored outcomes are `observed_mean`, with denominator and failure counts. Recovered outcomes remain separately identified and do not rewrite original operational success. Identical/cache-hit supplier trajectories are grouped as potentially dependent samples, with effective sample size/independence uncertainty stated. Do not combine historical best scores across configurations or treat within-case paraphrases as independent hosted evidence.

The existing D01/D02 suite has three repeats per arm, at least one score-point mean gain, at most two-point case regression, wins in at least two-thirds of repeat blocks, valid must-haves and known nonincreasing timeouts. Those are **implemented gates for that suite**, not evidence that D01/D02 establishes capacity quality. Retain them for that workflow. A capacity suite needs a reviewed manifest/case scope/budget; creating a new family must not evade prior quota limits.

Minimum evidence before making V2 the default for a scope:

1. All deterministic contract/fault/A–F gates pass; no validator bypass or unresolved-operation conflict; required suite/static checks complete with declared baseline issues resolved for the selected release.
2. Live-provider labelled interpreter results and protocol/latency/fallback evidence exist for the exact prompt/model/config when a live interpreter is part of the release.
3. Full frozen baseline/candidate outcome manifest with at least three original repeat blocks, known timing/invalid-action results, and no mixed config means. Repeats must have defensible independence; cached identical repeats alone are insufficient.
4. Pre-registered case-regression, mean-gain, timeout/runtime-failure and inference-cost limits are met. Add uncertainty estimates and sample limitations; deterministic gates alone are not a statistical significance claim.
5. Held-out category/supplier or independently varied negotiation evidence supports the intended scope. P10-only results can justify an opt-in P10/capacity pilot, not a broad default for all categories. If no additional independent capacity cases exist, record the generalization gap and retain pilot status.
6. Trace review confirms changes were commercially grounded, actual payload/cost is correct, and sustainability/basis uncertainty is disclosed internally. A good score cannot override a violated hard constraint.
7. Store a cited finding, experiment-log entry, approved source/config selection and tested rollback/recovery plan. Recommendation, code merge, deployment and default activation are separate operations.

No performance verdict is supplied by this planning task. If funded evidence is inconclusive, keep V2 opt-in and continue local research rather than treating architectural elegance as a measured win.

## 8. Lab integration and evaluation artifacts

Reuse Run/Attempt/campaign/fingerprint/gate records. Add versioned V2 trace attachments and a turn view showing evidence -> assessment -> intents -> rejected/approved candidates -> cost/scenarios -> selection -> validated payload -> submitted/acknowledged outcome -> feedback. Show the actual final payload rather than the initial pre-adviser decision. Filter/join by run/attempt/session/operation, not just case.

Required artifacts: contract fixture pack; annotated semantic corpus and split manifest; local correctness/fault report; behavior/ablation report; frozen launch-parity/config report; provider report when funded; original hosted session/attempt manifest when funded; promotion/rejection note and rollback record. Each artifact has source/config/schema hashes. JSONL remains convenient export; authoritative state/outcomes come from committed store records.

UI/report changes use existing Python and JavaScript tests and browser verification where appropriate. Do not create a second dashboard to get a V2 trace view. A report should explicitly show unsupported/model-fallback/recovery-required paths; missing metrics remain unknown, not zero.

Existing uncommitted audit, remediation, review, and documentation work is preserved. All V2 names and behavior below are proposals unless explicitly labelled as existing implementation.

## Recommendation

Build V2 alongside `PackageAgent` in `negotiator.v2`. Use one orchestrated decision loop with immutable inputs and typed contracts. Evidence, supplier interpretation, strategy proposal, candidate generation, economic evaluation, candidate selection, final validation, execution, and feedback have separate responsibilities. Keep official arithmetic and canonical claim verification behind independent interfaces. Preserve the raw observations so an alternative interpreter or strategy can use them later.

The first useful product is a **persistent, evidence-aware capacity negotiation loop**. Supplier delivery constraints, commitment requests, and explicit refusals must change its next commercial decision in an inspectable way. Begin with one case and one outstanding operation, a serial scheduling mode, deterministic wording, a bounded LLM interpreter, and deterministic candidate selection. An LLM selector can then be evaluated as a separate treatment. This keeps the initial intelligence demonstration small enough to verify.

Use existing readers, claims, arithmetic, experiment storage, and provenance patterns; replace their problematic integration boundaries. V2 does not depend on repairing every V1 module or implementing dormant scaffold functions. It does depend on a trustworthy economic adapter, shared evidence resolution, final action validation, honest terminal states, and durable operation ownership. Serial scheduling does not remove those obligations.

Strategies expose two interchangeable hooks: propose commercial intents and select an approved evaluated candidate. A strategy bundle can implement both hooks; research variants can iterate through a bounded, read-only candidate/evaluation service. They cannot execute, mutate facts, manufacture binding terms, or accept an offer. Closing eligibility and complete-cost comparison belong to a deterministic case coordinator.

V1 remains selectable and its historical results remain historical. A frozen V1 checkpoint is the comparison baseline; a V1 adapter through the new execution boundary is a distinct arm if it changes behavior. Promotion of V2 requires new evidence for one frozen configuration. The P10 adviser observation motivates the capacity slice; it does not establish V2 performance.

# C — Interface and domain specification

**Contract proposal:** `negotiator-v2/1`. No production implementation is supplied here. [Plan](../21-negotiation-v2-plan-2026-10-10.md) · [Architecture](B-architecture.md) · [Roadmap](D-roadmap.md).

This document is the common implementation handoff. Model tables specify fields omitted from the illustrative Python sketches. Changes to a field's meaning, source authority or outcome semantics require a recorded contract revision. First implement the minimal subset in M1; do not fabricate unsupported optional capabilities to satisfy a generic interface.

## 1. Universal contract rules

1. Boundary objects use strict, frozen Pydantic models, tuples, tagged unions, finite numbers and forbidden extra fields. Freeze nested values too; a frozen object containing a mutable dictionary is not immutable. Lists/maps may exist inside adapters but are converted before crossing a port.
2. Serialize versioned UTF-8 JSON. Decimal monetary/price values are canonical decimal strings in domain/storage JSON; dates are ISO dates, times are UTC with offset, and enums are strings. No NaN/infinity. Official Arena numeric JSON is generated only by its adapter using checked two-decimal values. Hash canonical sorted-key JSON with SHA-256; hashes exclude machine-local absolute roots, credentials and incidental receipt times unless time is part of the object's meaning.
3. Every durable envelope has `schema_version`. Stable content IDs identify evidence revisions, candidates and evaluations. UUIDs identify events, decisions, operations and attempts. Official IDs are opaque and session-scoped where appropriate; a `message_id` alone does not identify a message across sessions.
4. The only strategic-state writer is the coordinator through the state store. Components return values or proposed events. The only official-state writer is application of gateway observations. Components may keep bounded immutable caches; caches cannot change strategy after eviction or restart.
5. Typed results distinguish empty/infeasible/rejected/unknown/fallback/recovery-required/terminal. Missing data is never a numeric zero, no executable alternative is never mathematical infinity, and a proposed action is never a sent action.
6. A snapshot has a source `state_version` (event sequence), context/config/contract hashes, session identity and clock evidence. Candidates, evaluations and decisions bind to it. A stale object cannot authorize dispatch.
7. Significant assessment/intent/selection assertions cite existing message spans or evidence revisions. Validation can prove attribution and numeric calculations; human/local behavioral labels test semantic entailment. Rationale is an internal bounded summary, never executable code or private chain-of-thought.
8. Domain ports expose narrow capabilities. A strategy can evaluate hypothetical packages through a read-only port; it cannot access live transport, raw database handles, mutation methods, credentials or public results.

### IDs and immutable values

Use validated string wrappers/type aliases for `RunId`, `AttemptId`, `CaseId`, `SessionId`, `ThreadId`, `SupplierId`, `PartId`, `MessageId`, `OfferId`, `RecordId`, `ClaimId`, `IntentId`, `CandidateId`, `EvaluationId`, `DecisionId`, `EventId`, `OperationId`, `SourceVersion`, `ContextVersion`, `ConfigHash`, and `Sha256`. Official prefixes are not invented for provider/local objects. Candidate IDs hash `(contract, snapshot, intent, target, action contents)`; a matching package across turns has a separate `package_fingerprint` for refusal/repetition matching.

## 2. Core schemas

The sketches show the shape and important types. All auxiliary types are specified in the tables below; `core` may depend on standard Python and Pydantic only.

```python
from datetime import date, datetime
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import Annotated, Literal, Protocol
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

class FrozenModel(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(
        strict=True, frozen=True, extra="forbid", allow_inf_nan=False
    )

class PriceBasis(FrozenModel):
    currency: Literal["EUR"]
    price_unit: int                  # positive number of physical units per quoted price
    part_ids: tuple[str, ...]        # nonempty; basket basis must be explicitly declared
    quantity_basis: str              # validated ID of official case quantity convention
    source_refs: tuple[str, ...]

class Price(FrozenModel):
    amount: Decimal                 # finite, > 0; outbound tick is 0.01
    basis: PriceBasis

class Money(FrozenModel):
    amount: Decimal                 # finite; signed cost components allowed
    currency: Literal["EUR"] = "EUR"

class IndexClause(FrozenModel):
    series: str
    material_share: Decimal         # [0, 1]
    deadband_pct: Decimal            # >= 0
    base_month: str                  # YYYY-MM

TermField = Literal[
    "unit_price", "payment_days", "lead_time_days", "volume_per_year",
    "contract_months", "effective_date", "index_clause", "incoterm",
    "tooling_eur", "ppm_commitment", "chargeback_eur_per_complaint",
]
TermValue = int | Decimal | str | date | IndexClause | None

class TermBinding(FrozenModel):
    field: TermField
    value: TermValue                 # field-specific type validation, never bool-as-int

class Package(FrozenModel):
    bindings: tuple[TermBinding, ...] # unique fields; explicit null index_clause allowed
    price_basis: PriceBasis
    fingerprint: str                # canonical ordered bindings + basis

class SourceRef(FrozenModel):
    record_id: str                   # immutable evidence revision, not only canonical ID
    canonical_id: str | None = None

class MessageSpan(FrozenModel):
    session_id: str
    thread_id: str
    message_id: str
    start: int                       # Python Unicode character offsets
    end: int                         # exclusive; must reproduce exact quote
    quote: str

Citation = SourceRef | MessageSpan

class SnapshotRef(FrozenModel):
    run_id: str
    session_id: str
    state_version: int
    context_version: str
    config_hash: str
    case_contract_hash: str

class EvidenceRecord(FrozenModel):
    record_id: str
    canonical_id: str | None
    kind: Literal["canonical", "supplier_statement", "estimate", "hypothesis"]
    payload: "EvidencePayload"      # discriminated typed union specified below
    scope: "EvidenceScope"
    provenance: "Provenance"
    temporal: "TemporalValidity"
    disclosure: "DisclosureRule"

class GroundedObservation(FrozenModel):
    observation_id: str
    kind: Literal[
        "request", "refusal", "conditional_offer", "constraint",
        "approval_requirement", "stated_driver", "ambiguity"
    ]
    dimension: TermField | None
    summary: str
    citations: tuple[Citation, ...]  # nonempty
    package_fingerprint: str | None = None

class PreferenceHypothesis(FrozenModel):
    hypothesis_id: str
    dimension: TermField | None
    relation: Literal["prefers", "avoids", "requires", "unknown"]
    summary: str
    supporting_refs: tuple[Citation, ...]
    contradicting_refs: tuple[Citation, ...]
    confidence: Literal["low", "medium", "high", "unknown"]
    status: Literal["active", "stale", "superseded", "unknown"]
    numeric_effect: "EstimatedEffect | None" = None

class SupplierAssessment(FrozenModel):
    assessment_id: str
    supplier_id: str
    snapshot: SnapshotRef
    revision: int
    observations: tuple[GroundedObservation, ...]
    hypotheses: tuple[PreferenceHypothesis, ...]
    questions: tuple["ClarificationQuestion", ...]
    unknowns: tuple[str, ...]
    status: Literal["ok", "fallback", "insufficient_evidence"]
    interpreter_id: str
    model_call_id: str | None
    parent_assessment_id: str | None = None

class StrategyIntent(FrozenModel):
    intent_id: str
    strategy_id: str
    supplier_id: str
    snapshot: SnapshotRef
    kind: Literal["keep", "exchange", "evidence_challenge", "clarify", "request_close"]
    dimension: TermField | None
    direction: Literal["increase", "decrease", "enumerate", "unchanged"]
    observation_refs: tuple[str, ...]
    evidence_refs: tuple[SourceRef, ...]
    question_id: str | None
    rationale: str                  # internal, bounded
    supersedes_refusal_id: str | None = None

class OfferAction(FrozenModel):
    kind: Literal["offer"]
    packages: tuple[Package, ...]   # 1..3 complete outbound packages
    claim_ids: tuple[str, ...]
    question_id: str | None = None

class QuestionAction(FrozenModel):
    kind: Literal["question"]
    question_id: str

CandidateContents = Annotated[
    OfferAction | QuestionAction | CloseRequest, Field(discriminator="kind")

class CandidateAction(FrozenModel):

    intent_id: str

    snapshot: SnapshotRef

    evaluation_id: str

Package contains only explicitly transmitted negotiable terms. `ResolvedTerms` contains typed full bindings including closing defaults and each field's origin. ## 6. V1/V2 comparison and ablations

Name each treatment explicitly:

| Arm | Purpose |

Run a few chosen ablations that answer a specific question; do not spend budget on the full Cartesian product. Removing state/evidence for an ablation never removes hard validation or ownership. For offline fixed inputs, keep legal candidate universe/economic policies constant when isolating selector impact. For hosted studies, state/evidence/interpretation may change offered trajectories; record that and do not pretend replies are identical.

A benchmark manifest freezes source/kit/lock, data/release/prep hashes, case list, scenario/repeat order, agent/strategy/config/template/claim/interpreter/prompt/model versions, effort/sampling, model/server cache metadata, runner/key-owner policy, expected attempts, quota/spend ceiling, metrics and promotion criteria. tacto-negotiator/docs/v2/B-architecture.md:159:The model interpreter returns observations and separately labelled hypotheses. Code checks citation existence, supplier scope, exact message spans, enum values and schema; semantic correctness needs independent labels/tests. The initial capacity policy proposes intents only for supported dimensions, retains a baseline intent, and excludes known refused exchanges without new evidence. Candidate generation derives numeric prices/terms entirely in code and reports why an intent is infeasible. Candidate selection receives economic values and uncertainty as private decision inputs; an external model receives only the permitted projection in C.
tacto-negotiator/docs/v2/B-architecture.md:165:Use a versioned event log with a materialized `NegotiationState`. Events are immutable; snapshots are derived and replaceable. Each event has a run/session identity, unique event ID, monotone local sequence, parent/correlation IDs, source timestamp when available, receipt timestamp, schema version and typed payload. Deduplicate official messages by session/thread/message ID; if missing, use a documented stable fingerprint and flag ambiguity. Arrival order does not prove commercial causality.
tacto-negotiator/docs/v2/B-architecture.md:177:Persist raw observations plus bounded validated model artifacts; do not persist private chain-of-thought. Alternative interpreters can derive their own assessment revisions from the same source history. Strategy-specific memory is schema-versioned and namespaced; the first slice needs only generic attempted/refused-exchange records. It is not an untyped mutable blob.
tacto-negotiator/docs/v2/B-architecture.md:205:Incoming partial supplier sheets are preserved exactly as observed. # Main branch audit — 10 October 2026

## 1. Scope and overall assessment

Audited revision: **`3653046bce6dd7cbbeffe00ecf5dfd9c3edbc0ab`**, the checked-out `main` branch. The local `origin/main` reference points to the same revision. The checkout was clean before this review. I did not fetch the remote, so this identifies the available main snapshot, not a guarantee that GitHub has received no subsequent pushes.

The official kit is a submodule and a locked dependency at **`1b5516bb95ef28e37f69aa446dc62168864bca53`**. The review covers the custom buyer, official arithmetic/readers used by it, data package, configuration, serial and asynchronous execution, experiment Lab, deployment scripts, tests, and recorded experiments. No hosted negotiation, inference request, quota-consuming experiment, publication, or deployment was performed. Environment secret values were not needed for this analysis and are omitted.

**The implemented product is a deterministic procurement negotiator with optional evidence, experimental package trades, and a narrowly constrained LLM package selector.** It is accompanied by a substantial experiment platform. It does not implement the full model-driven writer, reply interpreter, supplier-belief engine, or offline planning system described in the architecture documents.

The strongest architectural choice is to calculate prices and complete-package costs in code and retain one closing decision function. The largest strategic limitation is that most rich supplier information either never enters the default decision path or is read without affecting the next move. The largest operational concerns are exceptional paths in asynchronous execution and inconsistent agent construction across launch paths.

The code is substantially more capable than the old scaffold checklist suggests. Equally, passing its tests does not establish all the runtime guarantees stated in the design. This review distinguishes:

- **Confirmed implementation:** directly followed in code.
- **Reproduced defect:** exercised offline during this audit.
- **Code-path risk:** the problematic behavior is visible, but its hosted consequence was not exercised.
- **Recorded measurement:** reported by existing experiment artifacts, not newly measured here.
- **Opportunity:** a plausible improvement requiring a controlled experiment.

## 2. What happens when it negotiates

### 2.1 Normal CLI launch

`negotiator play` and `negotiator run` load environment configuration through the official CLI helper. They load the packaged `src/negotiator/AGENTS.md` with `RuntimeGuidance.load()`, validate its JSON block, optionally load a `PolicyConfig`, construct a `PackageAgent`, and dispatch to the serial or async runner.

The runtime AGENTS file is executable configuration, not a model prompt. Its current values are:

| Setting | Current value | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `anchor` | 0.12 | Initial price reference is discounted by 12% |
| `rounds` | 5 | Five-step concession schedule |
| `close_gap` | 0.005 | Convergence threshold of 0.5% of the supplier reference price |
| `final_hold_s` | 40 | How long a leading final offer is held while another supplier remains open |
| `p_walk` | 0.25 | Assumed withdrawal probability when countering a final offer |
| `conditional_exchange` | true | Deterministic wording states that non-price terms are conditional on price |

The entire file hash and effective values appear in normal CLI run provenance. Prose and research links outside its structured settings do not alter policy.

The default runner is **serial**. The default agent does not call a model. Claims, dossier supplier estimates, and generic payment MESOs default off, unless enabled through their environment switches or an explicit policy.

Sources: [CLI](../src/negotiator/cli.py), [runtime guidance loader](../src/negotiator/guidance.py), [packaged settings](../src/negotiator/AGENTS.md), [agent initialization](../src/negotiator/agent.py).

### 2.2 Opening and document handling

Opening a session returns the case and supplier threads. Opening PDFs and later attachments are downloaded and converted to text by official readers. PDFs use `pypdf`; XLSX files use `openpyxl`, with formula strings retained rather than recalculated.

The code searches the latest quote attachment for its **standard terms**. Those standards supply omitted closing fields. The official resolution order implemented by `closing_terms` is:

1. Buyer-plan defaults.
2. Quote standard terms.
3. Case fixed terms.
4. Explicit offer terms.

This precedence is significant: the case's fixed terms override standards, and explicit sheet terms override both in the arithmetic. Offer-schema enforcement must therefore keep unauthorized fields from entering the sheet.

The PDF parser recognizes specific labels and section headings. The policy consumes the parsed standard section; it does not generally mine all attachment content for commercial signals. Downloading a cost-breakdown workbook does not mean its cost elements are used.

Sources: [serial loop](../src/negotiator/play.py), [async document handling](../src/negotiator/runner.py), official `arena_kit/docs.py` and `arena_kit/cost.py`.

### 2.3 Candidate terms and price negotiation

For each supplier, the agent considers priced sheets in its latest message, checks must-haves, and calculates complete costs. It distinguishes the supplier's first, standing sheet from other alternatives. Alternatives can be copied into a counteroffer, but are not accepted directly by ID.

On its first ordinary offer, `best_terms` enumerates combinations of permitted non-price options at a supplied reference price and chooses the cheapest compliant combination. This is a finite enumeration over terms, not a search over all possible prices or supplier acceptance behavior.

The agent generally retains its previous non-price package. It can adopt a cheaper supplier package when the supplier has actually quoted the previous package at a worse complete cost. It also adopts individual supplier-requested changes when they preserve must-haves and do not increase buyer cost at the same price.

The price concession schedule is essentially:

```text
floor = opening-package-equivalent price × (1 − 0.12)
proposal = floor + (current reference price − floor) × min(1, offers_sent / 5)
```

The code converts prices between packages using a numerical inverse of total cost. It tries to avoid backtracking on its own concessions in cost terms, limits proposals to the supplier reference, and can cap a rival's offer below a leading final offer.

When the buyer/supplier price gap becomes small, it can re-offer its own terms at the supplier's price, convert a cheaper alternative sheet into a counteroffer, or request a case close.

This is a rule-based negotiation schedule. The default path does not learn supplier preferences, estimate a concession curve, update withdrawal probabilities, or decide whether a particular argument worked.

Sources: [agent package and decision logic](../src/negotiator/agent.py), [optimizer](../src/negotiator/optimizer.py), [inverse pricing and sheet evaluation](../src/negotiator/evaluator.py).

### 2.4 Optional deterministic package trades

An explicit policy can enable `TradePolicy` for selected case types. It can:

- Evaluate opening package combinations at the anchored price as well as the quoted price.
- Recognize the historical `multi_year_only` trait and propose an allowed longer commitment.
- Use configured supplier-standard payment terms.
- Relax quality or chargeback terms according to allowed options and the configured experiment.
- Detect stagnation from three supplier price surfaces.
- Switch one relevant package dimension, with at most two non-price switches, enough remaining moves, and a nominal 20-second time check.

Its stagnation switch order is predetermined. It uses only a small subset of the many available traits. Payment switching is triggered by a specific trait or literal English phrases. Commitment, quality, chargeback, and index-clause switches follow fixed rules.

`revealed_deltas` calculates one-field price differences between supplier sheets, but those differences are currently logged rather than used as a learned supplier valuation model.

The longer-lead flag adds a tie-break: when legal opening packages have exactly the same complete cost, prefer a longer lead time. It has recorded capacity-case evidence and remains opt-in.

Sources: [trade policy](../src/negotiator/trades.py), [policy schema](../src/negotiator/policy.py), [lead-time tie-break](../src/negotiator/optimizer.py).

### 2.5 Evidence selection and sending

Evidence is appended to an already generated move. `EvidencePolicy` constructs a case-scoped context, verifies canonical claims, selects at most three, appends their sentences, and attaches their IDs.

By default the evidence feature is restricted to single-supplier price-increase cases. An explicit policy can enable other types, but the single-supplier restriction remains. The combined candidate enables evidence for price-increase and quality cases.

The claim machinery supports index changes, supplier scorecards, notice periods, rival quotes, live-offer claim records, and should-cost estimates. Actual automatic delivery is narrower:

- Only buyer-supporting claims are selected by default.
- Adverse facts remain candidates for internal inspection.
- Cherry-picked index windows are generated and flagged, but excluded by default.
- Internal should-cost claims are not sent.
- Rival disclosure is excluded by the default disclosure set.
- RFQs do not pass the current evidence eligibility gate.
- The live-offer helper is not wired into automatic selection from current session offers.

The canonical renderer and checker are a strong improvement: changing a claim figure without changing its sentence fails verification. Notice claims check supplier, part applicability, dates, the trigger letter, and the contract's required period. Scorecard sentences correctly describe supplier-wide rolling metrics rather than claiming part-specific performance.

Used IDs are reconstructed from buyer-history `refs`, and proposed claims are reserved in memory before sending. Failed or unsent proposals can therefore consume evidence conservatively. This avoids easy duplicates but may waste useful claims. The code does not adapt evidence selection from the supplier's returned `claim_results`.

Sources: [evidence delivery](../src/negotiator/evidence.py), [context](../src/negotiator/context.py), [claims](../src/negotiator/claims.py).

### 2.6 Closing

`close_decision` owns the final economic comparison. It selects the cheapest acceptable standing sheet across live threads whose complete cost is strictly below the supplied alternative's cost. If none qualifies, it walks away.

This shared evaluator is used for ordinary closes, `agreed`, final offers, exhausted moves, and wave-deadline fallback. A supplier saying `agreed` therefore does not bypass economic checks.

A missing usable alternative price is represented as infinity. That lets finite valid deals pass the comparison, but it also creates infinite loss in some final-counter risk calculations. It is important to distinguish three quantities: an executable alternate offer, operational fallback procurement, and the arena score for no deal. They are not interchangeable.

For final offers, the policy normally allows at most one counter, estimates potential gain against loss if the supplier withdraws, and uses the fixed `p_walk=0.25`. An optional `opening_proxy` mode provides an opening-relative heuristic for cases without an alternate quote. It is explicitly a proxy, not expected normalized score.

Sources: [closing evaluator](../src/negotiator/evaluator.py), [final-offer logic](../src/negotiator/agent.py), [alternative cost](../src/negotiator/optimizer.py).

The arrow from release data to dossiers has a boundary: merged news/doc IDs can be read, but many dossier fields still come from base SQLite queries. Case dossier enrichment currently adds new case news only. The arrow through the model exists only for the explicitly enabled serial selector.

Authority is distributed sensibly in the ordinary path:

| Input | What it may influence | What it cannot authorize |
|---|---|---|
| Case schema, fixed terms, buyer rates and must-haves | Legal options and economic evaluation | Arbitrary fields outside the case |
| Supplier standing term sheet | A possible acceptance | Automatic acceptance without checks |
| Other supplier sheets | Counteroffer candidates | Direct acceptance of a non-standing ID |
| Quote standard terms | Defaults for omitted closing fields | Bypassing the case schema |
| Facts and contracts | Canonical verified claims | Executable instructions |
| Notes, news and supplier prose | Traits, relevance, optional model choice | Inventing binding terms or new facts |
| Model output | Selection of a code-approved package ID | Pricing, custom claims, free-form outgoing prose, closing |
| Historical scores, Cbest and public board | Human evaluation and experiments | Runtime strategy targets |

The live input path does not read the public benchmark artifacts for strategy. Async requests block listed spectator endpoint paths. The serial buyer currently calls permitted methods, but its underlying official client exposes leaderboard/backoffice methods and has no equivalent custom endpoint guard; separation depends on call-site discipline.

## 4. Economic evaluation: what is deterministic

The official cost function includes:

| Component | Data used |
|---|---|
| Price | Commitment quantity, covered duration, unit price, current price, effective date |
| Uncovered need | Fixed demand, fixed horizon, committed coverage, fallback unit price |
| Fallback risk | Uncovered cost and category-specific percentage |
| Payment | Actual spend, buyer rate, reference days, agreed days |
| Freight | Committed quantity and Incoterm cost map |
| Late delivery | Days beyond buyer need and daily penalty |
| Quality | Committed quantity, ppm, defect cost less capped chargeback |
| Tooling | Agreed tooling amount |
| Index clause | Published buyer index path, material share, deadband |
| Index risk | Published risk percentage and indexed exposure |
| Relationship | Estimated supplier cash value, full cost, sustainable margin and goal penalty |

The relationship component is zero locally without a supplier estimate. This is especially consequential for `stabilise` and `secure_supply` cases: a mechanically cheaper deal can be worse under the supplier-health penalty used in scoring.

Supplier estimates are hypotheses built from should-cost, master terms, scorecards, and traits. Assumed rates are 8% normally, 15% for cash-short suppliers, and 20% for liquidity crisis. When should-cost is absent, the estimator assumes a 6% margin on the current price. It records an uncertainty interval, but the live decision code uses the point estimate; it does not optimize or report decisions over the interval.

The following are deterministic: file loading, facts merging, regex traits, option enumeration, complete-cost arithmetic, offer ranking, most package switches, price scheduling, claim rendering/checking/picking, template messages, shared closing, request journals, Lab gates, and score summaries. Deterministic buyer code can still receive stochastic supplier replies. Optional model calls also introduce variability, and time-dependent decisions depend on runtime conditions.

The code does not deploy or train a pricing model, fine-tune a language model, or run an autonomous multi-agent deliberation system. Workers are orchestration tasks, not independent LLM decision agents.

### 5.1 What is intentionally excluded

The agent intentionally keeps internal budgets, reservation costs, target prices, lack of alternatives, urgency, should-cost estimates, unverified weighted aggregates, adverse claims, and rival quotes out of default outward messaging. Most of these are sensible disclosure constraints.

That does not justify leaving the same data unused internally. In particular, adverse commodity data should affect the buyer's assessment of a credible ask even if it is not sent as a concessionary argument. The current policy does not use those facts to update its mechanical 12% opening anchor.

The dossier builder excludes five named document subjects: holiday shutdown, new contact person, ISO certificate, packaging, and trade-fair invitation. Some are likely noise, but shutdown, certification and packaging could be operationally relevant in a future logistics/quality case. Exclusion should be case-aware.

### 5.2 Offline preparation is not on the live dependency path

`negotiator prep` writes `experiments/prep.json`. Other tools write dossier exports and sensitivity analyses. There is no reader of `prep.json` in the live buyer.

When enabled, evidence and estimates rebuild data structures from the package at runtime. `TradePolicy.prepare` can run before opening in the async runner if metadata is available. In the serial path, dossier preparation may happen during the first decision after clocks start. Evidence contexts recursively hash package files and construct claims/dossiers on the live path. Each separately constructed agent can repeat work.

This is both a missed latency improvement and a misleading aspect of the apparent pipeline: running prep does not automatically make the subsequent negotiation consume the prepared evidence.

### 6.1 The real optional model selector

`PackageAdvisor` calls an OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` endpoint using `LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_API_KEY`, `LLM_MODEL`, and optionally `LLM_EFFORT`. It does not branch on `LLM_PROVIDER`. It requests strict JSON-schema output and uses `max_completion_tokens`, unlike the connectivity probe's simpler `max_tokens` protocol. A successful probe therefore does not prove the adviser protocol is supported.

Code generates legal one-field package variants for payment, commitment, lead time, and index clause, triggered by broad keyword signals. Candidates must meet the scheduled package's buyer-cost ceiling. Price reductions compensate expensive term changes when inverse pricing is safe. Previously proposed packages and a two-switch history budget limit repetition.

The model sees the latest supplier body (up to 6,000 characters), up to eight recent messages, approved terms, scheduled terms, and up to twelve note texts (2,000 characters each). Buyer cost estimates, reservation costs, targets and score benchmarks are not supplied as structured fields. Notes are copied through a constrained interface, although the content of historical notes still needs appropriate data handling.

The model returns `selected_id` and `supporting_quote`. A changed package needs an exact substring of the latest reply of at least eight characters. Code rechecks legality and cost, then sends a fixed template and the selected sheet. No model-written prose is sent.

The call has an eight-second total waiting bound and a process-wide semaphore of four model calls. Timed-out daemon calls may continue until their HTTP operation exits; they are not forcibly cancelled. Missing credentials, errors, invalid output or unsupported quotations fall back to the deterministic move. Final offers, actions, multiple sheets, existing evidence refs, or less than 20 nominal seconds remaining skip advice.

The current adviser is enabled by `configs/package-advice.json` for **capacity only**. The async runner rejects an agent with this feature before opening a session. This means the measured semantic improvement cannot currently be combined with the async final runner by merely adding a flag.

The exact-quote check proves provenance of a substring, not that the selected exchange is commercially sensible. Avoiding a refused package and understanding role authority remain model judgments. Structured output protects numeric/action authority but does not prove semantic correctness.

### 6.2 The separate connection probe

`InferenceProbeAgent` inherits deterministic economics. At most once per case it sends a fixed prompt containing no supplier or private procurement data. It accepts only `concise` or `collaborative` and appends the corresponding fixed phrase. It records call/fallback counts and elapsed times.

It is useful for endpoint connectivity and response-shape checks. It does not read a supplier, choose an economic trade, deploy a model, or validate the package-adviser protocol. Its 0.1–5-second HTTP timeout is a phase timeout, not a hard total move deadline.

### 6.3 Lab cloud hosting

The Azure documentation and experiment log record a deployment on an Ubuntu VM, with Caddy terminating HTTPS and the Python Lab bound to loopback port 8000. Its persistent store is SQLite. Those are recorded deployment observations; I did not contact the VM during this audit.

The current `main` CI workflow also deploys the Lab to a Nebius VM at the hostname documented in `ops/nebius/README.md`. On pushes to main it runs Lab-server tests and Ruff, archives tracked project source, sends it over pinned SSH, installs locked dependencies into a revision release, switches a `current` symlink, restarts the service, and rolls back if the local health check fails. Data and credentials remain outside the archive under `/var/lib/y-agent-lab`.

That workflow deploys the **dashboard**, not buyer agents or model weights. Deployment tests cover `test_lab_server.py`, not the entire negotiation suite. The local health check expects unauthenticated `/api/runs` to return 401; the external check fetches the root page. Neither proves a negotiation policy is operational or that a specific revision is serving after every possible deployment race.

The repo still contains laptop-tunnel, Azure, and Nebius connection instructions. There is no single canonical active endpoint encoded across them. A teammate following the inference setup doc can still get an old tunnel endpoint. Which host is currently used by each teammate and what revision is live require operational verification outside this code review.

Sources: [Nebius deployment](../../ops/nebius/README.md), [CI workflow](../../.github/workflows/deploy-nebius-lab.yml), [deployment script](../../ops/nebius/deploy-lab.sh), [Azure runbook](15-azure-lab-hosting.md), [inference setup](17-inference-setup.md).

The checkpoint configuration schema only accepts the basic schedule values, `meso`, `claims`, and `estimates`. The worker also hardcodes `PackageAgent`; it cannot select `InferenceProbeAgent` through a checkpoint.

Therefore the current immutable campaign mechanism cannot express the newly added policy improvements through its existing config. A Lab recommendation also does not automatically activate a normal CLI agent: normal play/run does not read the recommendation registry.

An explicit policy overrides `claims` based on whether `evidence_types` is nonempty. With an evidence policy loaded, passing `claims=False` or setting the claims environment flag off does not disable those policy-enabled types. Conversely a policy with no evidence types turns claims off. This is implemented precedence that must be made visible in experiment records and commands.

## 8. Confirmed defects and operational risks

### F1 — Inverse price search fails with supplier-health penalties

**Severity: high when supplier estimates are enabled. Reproduced offline.**

`price_for_cost` assumes total cost rises monotonically with price and binary-searches from zero. Relationship cost invalidates that assumption: lowering the price can increase the supplier-health penalty faster than it reduces buyer spend. The trade policy and package adviser recognize this and disable some inversions with estimates, but the main agent's `_ask_on`, concession conversion, final-counter logic, and payment variants still use this function with supplier estimates.

Using the existing `STABILISE` test fixture and its supplier estimate:

| Unit price | Complete cost |
|---:|---:|
| 20 | €1,534,600.00 |
| 30 | €831,266.67 |
| 40 | €519,600.00 |
| 45 | €429,044.44 |
| 48 | €397,273.61 |
| 49 | €401,600.00 |
| 55 | €449,600.00 |

Inverting the valid target cost €401,600 returned **price 0.0**. Evaluating that returned price caused **`ZeroDivisionError`** in supplier margin arithmetic. A valid price of 49 was already available.

Keep the fast inverse for proven monotonic cases. For relationship cases, use a positive-domain search that identifies feasible cost intervals and roots, or enumerate a bounded price grid and refine appropriate intervals. Define behavior when the target is below the minimum possible cost. Validate every resulting price and cost before sending.

Source: [evaluator, `price_for_cost`, line 88](../src/negotiator/evaluator.py); [agent callers](../src/negotiator/agent.py); official relationship arithmetic.

### F2 — A failed close can be recorded as a finished case while the server is still open

**Severity: high. Reproduced offline.**

After three close attempts, `CaseRunner._close` fetches server state and calls `_end` with a fallback result even if the server still reports `status='open'`. This does not prove an accept or walk-away occurred.

Offline reproduction with a fake server rejecting each close with 422:

```text
server status: open
local ended: true
local result: {deal: false, end_reason: null}
```

The normal `run()` path can then write that result into the journal and abandon pending intents. A future launch using the same journal can return the local result without resuming the still-open server session. The CLI generally treats the missing score as failure, which helps visibility, but the internal terminal-state claim is wrong.

Only record completed/ended after authoritative terminal state or a confirmed close response. Preserve an unresolved operational state after exhausted attempts and keep recovery possible.

Source: [runner, close fallback, line 531](../src/negotiator/runner.py), [run result journalling, line 567](../src/negotiator/runner.py).

### F3 — An unhandled worker error can strand an async run

**Severity: high. Reproduced offline.**

`run()` creates worker tasks but awaits the watchdog first. If a worker raises during proposal generation, attachment processing, or another unhandled operation, its error is not supervised. The thread can remain marked workable or in flight. The watchdog need not observe a condition that ends the case.

With an offline agent whose `propose` raises `ValueError`, the worker terminated, the runner remained pending, the thread remained workable, and Python reported an uncollected task exception. In practice/sandbox, there may be no wave deadline to rescue it. In a final wave, the cap can eventually intervene, but much of the usable time has already been lost.

Supervise worker completion/errors, reconcile server state, and explicitly fail or safely close the case. Cancel/gather remaining tasks in a guaranteed cleanup path. Distinguish recoverable thread failures from a case-wide invalid economic evaluator.

Source: [runner, worker line 340 and run line 553](../src/negotiator/runner.py).

### F4 — Supplier estimates retain stale master standards over current quote standards

**Severity: high for relationship estimates. Reproduced offline.**

`supplier_for` uses `est.get('standard') or standard`, so any nonempty estimate standard suppresses the current quote PDF's standard dictionary. Dossier estimates normally supply a nonempty standard.

Providing an estimate with payment 60/FCA and a current quote with payment 30/DAP returned the estimate standards **60/FCA**. Supplier cash value is then measured against the wrong payment/freight reference. This contradicts the estimator's documented instruction to override master defaults with current quote terms.

Merge defaults and current quote standards field by field, with quote fields taking precedence. Test the resulting supplier value and relationship penalty, not just the dictionary shape.

## 9. Strategic opportunities and underused evidence

### 9.1 Supplier willingness must complement buyer-cost optimization

The baseline chooses the cheapest non-price terms at a reference price and then asks for cheaper prices. That can yield packages the supplier has no reason to accept. The recorded P04 example demonstrates this clearly: the baseline kept a 12-month package while supplier notes identified multi-year agreements as the discount lever. The package experiment changed that and materially improved the recorded score.

The same issue appears with fast payment, constrained capacity, hedged material costs, fixed lists, and approval committees. The relevant data already exists. The next useful engine would generate a small number of supplier-plausible trades from case-valid fields, estimate buyer cost in code, and choose which trade to test based on the actual reply. It should not simply enable every trait globally.

### 9.2 Turn observed package prices into valuations

The code already has complete supplier sheets and one-field revealed deltas. Use them to estimate supplier premiums for payment, contract length, freight and delivery, with uncertainty. Compare a quote-supported trade against hypothetical equal-buyer-cost packages. When sheets change several fields, retain that as a combined observation rather than falsely attributing its entire price difference to one field.

`beliefs.py` would be a natural place for this, but its update and prior functions are currently stubs. A small deterministic observation record could deliver value before a sophisticated model is needed.

### 9.3 Ask useful questions and use requested documents

The message contract permits question-only moves. The policy mostly emits attached packages and does not implement a question strategy. `Move.question` is scaffolded, but `next_move` is a stub.

Open-book traits and recorded supplier notes provide a specific reason to request a cost breakdown. Logistics and quality roles can return delivery schedules and 8D reports. Currently the buyer downloads these attachments but does not systematically extract facts that change its next proposal.

Add a bounded document-request action only when its expected information value exceeds a scarce round and timing cost. Parse known workbook structures deterministically. Keep rendered financial figures separate from untrusted prose.

### 9.4 Use adverse data internally

P01's claim bank preserves rising wages and material indices, but their effect stops largely at inspection. The weighted cost-pressure helper estimates only partial cost coverage and is appropriately marked unverified. It should not become a claim that the entire ask is unjustified.

It could still help internally: acknowledge which drivers rose, distinguish hedged versus spot exposure, and ask a specific question about uncovered cost components. Avoid turning partial weighted index arithmetic into a hard reservation price.

### 9.5 Payment evidence should drive a bounded trade

The dossier calculates average lateness across paid invoices, mixing early and late payments. That can hide important cash-flow behavior. The provided research example filters out discounted invoices; the runtime dossier does not. Supplier aliases are not aggregated.

Use distributions of lateness, overdue exposure, legitimate versus late discounts, and linked invoice quantities to assess whether payment timing is a credible lever. Offer a schema-valid exchange and compare complete costs. Recorded D02 MESO regression is a reason to limit and test this feature rather than roll it out indiscriminately.

### 9.6 Multi-part and supplier-account context is thin

Claim generation, cost-driver lookup, and supplier estimates select `case['parts'][0]`. P07 and P15 contain multiple parts. Case-level basket economics can still be evaluated using the published aggregate schema, but the agent lacks corresponding basket evidence and account-level leverage.

Build a scoped basket context across all parts, and keep supplier-wide metrics distinct from part-specific claims. Account importance from spend and sourcing can guide commitment dialogue without promising unauthorized volume.

### 9.7 Evidence quality and usefulness are different objectives

The new evidence context records source layers, hashes, units, failures and gaps. This is valuable for inspectability. Its signals are explicitly classifier hypotheses with unchecked freshness and do not automatically change policy.

Add a feedback record joining each sent claim with `verified`, `contradicted`, `irrelevant` or `duplicate`, the supplier's explanation, and subsequent package movement. Do not interpret verification as proof of persuasion. Existing general thresholds, such as OTD below 90%, may miss case-relevant leverage between 90% and the 95% target.
